title: FileStatusChanged.v1
description: Payload of the FileStatusChanged event — an ingestion-internal catalogue extension beyond the 22 A§23 events (plan §6.5). Emitted by the ingestion control plane — the single producer — once per file-registry state transition, mirroring the append-only `file_state_transition` audit row that is written in the same transaction (A§36, D§20, D§3.6: the audit is INSERT + SELECT only, and this event is its published projection). Published on `ingestion.file.lifecycle.v1` keyed by `fileId`, so the whole lifecycle of one file is strictly ordered (A§26). Consumed by Airflow sensors and the operational dashboard, never by domain services: domain services consume only the canonical `ingestion.{customers,accounts,debts,payments}.v1` topics (plan §6.2). Rides the A§24 envelope; a breaking change ships as FileStatusChanged.v2 (D§29).

fileId.description: File registry identifier: the `FIL_` prefix followed by a bare ULID, e.g. `FIL_01M0KK53S0DQ9PSTK0206PRD7M` (operational entities carry a type prefix — docs/conventions.md §1). Equal to the envelope `aggregateId` and the Kafka partition key. Declared with an explicit pattern rather than reusing the envelope's bare-ULID definition precisely because of the prefix.

feedId.description: Identifier of the feed this file belongs to, as declared in the feed contract under `contracts/files/<feedId>.v1.yaml` (D§81). Lower snake_case, owned by the ingestion configuration rather than minted as a ULID, so a human reading an alert can tell which feed broke.

sourceId.description: Identifier of the source system the feed belongs to (A§28.1 `source` registry entry). Lower snake_case, configuration-owned like `feedId`.

fileName.description: File name exactly as received from the source, before any normalisation — the value the `UNIQUE(feedId, fileName)` dedup constraint and the A§33 filename-reuse quarantine rule are evaluated on, so it must never be rewritten.

businessDate.description: Business date the file's content belongs to, as an ISO calendar date (YYYY-MM-DD). Feeds carry it as YYYYMMDD in the file name and header because the source systems emit it that way (contracts/files/*.v1.yaml); it is normalised to an ISO date here so every consumer parses one format. This is the date reconciliation, backfills and Airflow data intervals key on — not the arrival time.

fromStatus.description: Registry status before this transition, or null for the very first transition of a file (its discovery, which has no predecessor state). Structurally always present, so required and nullable. Same closed vocabulary as `toStatus`.

toStatus.description: Registry status reached by this transition. Exactly the twelve A§36 ingestion states, no more and no fewer: the happy path DISCOVERED -> RECEIVED -> VALIDATING -> VALIDATED -> PROCESSING -> PROCESSED -> RECONCILING -> RECONCILED -> ARCHIVED, with FAILED, QUARANTINED and DUPLICATE as the exception paths. Closed enum because the transition map is table-driven and an unknown state is an ingestion bug, not an extension: a file reaches ARCHIVED only after a reconciliation PASS, a checksum repeat is terminal DUPLICATE, and a filename reuse with different content is QUARANTINED (A§33).

reason.description: Why the transition happened, or null for an unremarkable happy-path step. Mandatory in content terms for every exception transition — FAILED, QUARANTINED and DUPLICATE must always carry one, because an unexplained quarantine cannot be triaged from the alert alone. Open SCREAMING_SNAKE vocabulary shared with the registry's `error_code` column (e.g. FILENAME_REUSED per A§33).

at.description: When the transition was recorded in the append-only audit, RFC3339 UTC with a `Z` offset. Equal to the envelope `occurredAt` for a transition published as it happens; it is carried explicitly so that a lifecycle republished from the audit table (backfill or DLQ replay, D§48/§49) still states the original transition time rather than the republication time.
